Use case: ui-mockup Asset type: ONE fully designed core webpage for the Ferromark / Ferroni family, coherent design development of selected concepts 11 and 14. Canvas: a TALL full-page DESKTOP screenshot, around 1440px width by 3000px height, from header to footer. This is a complete long webpage, not only a hero, not a phone screen, no browser or device chrome, no external concept-board labels. Maintain readable text and natural desktop proportions. Input images: image 1 is the approved full project homepage STYLE REFERENCE; image 2 is the selected Calibration sheet STYLE REFERENCE. Image 3 is the project's meaningful OBJECT REFERENCE. Reuse its identity and mechanical logic rather than replacing it with a generic sculpture. Shared visual system: light theme ONLY everywhere, including code, header and footer. Warm white #FCFCF8, white #FFFFFF, fine silver #D4D8D6, pale neutral #ECEDE7, readable graphite #3D423E, controlled oxide #965332. Fine brushed satin steel, tiny countersunk screws, clean stabilized rust. Fine mechanisms and carefully made parts, generous white space, no thick frames or factory props. Small text always on flat surfaces. Minimal surface texture. Softer regular-width industrial humanist sans, mostly regular and medium weights; moderate headline size, no huge bold project word. Monospace only for code and numerical data. Sentence case throughout. Family cohesion: same white 64px header, text project wordmark at left, navigation Overview / Start with Rust / core topic / Benchmarks / GitHub; a quiet Ferramenta family link at right. Restrained thin oxide active underline. Same pale rules, code panels, install line, comparison tables and compact white family footer across pages. Do not invent a brand logo or use the Rust logo as the project logo; use clean text wordmarks and a small text "Rust-native" marker where appropriate. Content: render the supplied headings, essential sentences, code and numbers accurately in US English. Use short readable prose. Facts below are approved design content, never reproduce these design instructions as visible copy. No fabricated API methods, claims, quotes, customer logos, version numbers, tests, metrics or unlabeled invented chart values. Material objects are explanatory metaphors, not claims about literal software architecture. No family-wide pipeline diagram. Avoid dark bands, dark editors, dirty rust, grunge, molten metal, anvils, huge gears, heavy bolts, steampunk pipework, shiny chrome glare, all-caps shouting, huge Rust cog branding, identical marketing card grids, illegible microtext and cropped-off footer. Page: Ferromark / Start with Rust Composition: A complete documentation landing page in the same identity. White family header, then a slim 190px left documentation index and wide readable content column, with a narrow right-side "On this page" anchor list. No large hero photo. A small cropped detail of the source document entering the register sits alongside the page introduction, taking less than 12% of the content area. Main body has numbered install/run steps only where sequence is real, a wide light Rust code panel and real output. Then a clear open API-choice table and pale oxide trust-policy callout. Bottom next-page links are flat and editorial. Preserve generous spacing and readable code; this should feel like a carefully set technical manual. Correct header wordmark: Ferromark. Core-topic header label: Rendering. Visible content, including exact code: # Start with Rust Render your first document, then choose the API your pipeline needs. ## Install cargo add ferromark ## Render your first document fn main() -> Result<(), ferromark::ParseError> { let html = ferromark::to_html("Hello, **world**!")?; println!("{html}"); Ok(()) } Output:

Hello, world!

## Choose your API Task | API Render one document | to_html() Choose syntax and output policy | to_html_with_options() Append to an existing string | to_html_into() Inspect document structure | Allocator + Parser + HtmlRenderer Customize output | HtmlRenderHooks ## Choose your trust policy Rust preserves raw HTML by default. For untrusted Markdown, enable HtmlRendererOptions::sanitize. The Node.js API has different defaults. Read the rendering policy before accepting untrusted input. ## Continue Rendering and metadata Benchmarks API reference Ferromark · Part of Ferramenta · GitHub · Imprint · Privacy Preserve the code's backslashes and API spellings verbatim. Use only these snippets; do not invent additional code. Maintain spacious desktop documentation proportions.
